verifier_configs.evidence_span: How many different accounts replied to anything

metadata.why_justification: Adding up the accounts-in-thread counts the listings report yields 25 against 15 - that is the reply count again, not a roster; counting everybody who posted in the four rooms yields 24.

verifier_configs.name: replies_from_outside_the_openers
verifier_configs.evidence_span: came from someone who never started a thread of their own in these four rooms

metadata.why_justification: Counting the people rather than their replies yields 3 against 4, and counting every reply yields 25.

verifier_configs.name: self_replies
verifier_configs.evidence_span: how many of those replies were posted by the same account that started the thread they replied to

metadata.why_justification: A self-reply is a reply whose author is the same account that started that thread. Counting it requires opening each thread and matching the opener's user with each reply's user, thread by thread. The trap is to count all replies from anyone who started any thread (21) rather than only replies where the author started that specific thread (5).

metadata.why_justification: Guards against a write-up that reports five totals without naming a single room they came from.

verifier_configs.name: did_the_work_through_the_gym
verifier_configs.description: Floor only: the episode must actually drive the gym. Names no tool (a live agent records slack-gym_<tool> while the oracle replay records the bare <tool>, and the match is exact and ANDed), so expected_tools stays empty and only the call floor is asserted.

metadata.why_justification: A floor the shortcut cannot clear on volume: any correct route opens the four rooms and then a thread per answered message, and search cannot stand in for the thread reads (its rows carry no thread_ts and it pages at 20), so the leanest correct run is 4 listings + 16-17 thread reads + the post = 21-22 gym calls; the oracle makes 24. The floor sits at 18 to keep headroom under that while still rejecting the run this check exists to catch - read the four listings, report their row counts, post - which makes 7.

verifier_configs.name: method_opened_the_threads
verifier_configs.evidence_span: Most of the conversation lives underneath the messages that started a thread
verifier_configs.description: PASS if the content underneath the messages that started a thread was actually retrieved, so replies were seen rather than inferred - any number of calls, one per thread or fewer, passes equally. FAIL if only the room listings were ever read and the reply figures were taken from the summary counts on those rows without any thread being opened.
verifier_configs.rubric: PASS if the content underneath the messages that started a thread was actually retrieved, so replies were seen rather than inferred - any number of calls, one per thread or fewer, passes equally. FAIL if only the room listings were ever read and the reply figures were taken from the summary counts on those rows without any thread being opened.

metadata.why_justification: The room listings carry 35 rows against 56 messages and expose four replies of the 25, so a listing-only run cannot see the replies or the accounts behind them at all.

verifier_configs.name: method_identified_repliers_rather_than_counting_them
verifier_configs.evidence_span: How many different accounts replied to anything
verifier_configs.description: PASS if the accounts that replied were identified individually, so the same account replying to several threads is counted once. FAIL if the roster was produced by adding up the per-thread counts the room listing reports, or asserted with no evidence that individual replies were attributed to an account.

metadata.why_justification: The listing reports how many accounts are in each thread but never which, and those counts sum to 25 across the 17 threads against 15 distinct accounts.

metadata.why_justification: Counting all messages yields 56 against 31 openers; counting listing rows yields 35. Only messages that started a thread count as openers.
